proof_state.restore_id: SHA-256 of ordered JSON event fields excluding restore_id
proof_state.parent_receipt_id: same-subject committed receipt whose exact checkpoint bytes and manifest were revalidated before staged WASM import
proof_state.state_parent_receipt_id: immediate prior committed state: the restored parent for the first run, then the preceding successful run of this session
proof_state.restore_event_id: the host-committed event that selected this session's checkpoint; present on all descendant receipts until create or another restore replaces the session
proof_state.other_ancestry: state handoff binds external output to a later signed state input independently of internal ProgramBundle ancestry

valid_transitions: trusted startup --allow-checkpoint-restore enables op=restore independently of --allow-state-checkpoint-export
host loads a same-subject committed receipt and private retained bytes, checks byte and manifest digests, stages WASM import, and validates structural identity and logical ports
host commits the restore event under the ledger lock before replacing the live session; a failed event commit leaves the old session intact
the new session starts without input tensors or signed proofs; a successful run records the restored parent receipt and restore event ID
subsequent successful runs advance the immediate state parent while retaining the same restore event ID
if numerical execution began and a later operation fails, the host discards that session because its mutable state may have changed without a committed receipt
ledger reopening validates restore ID, parent receipt, execution-order anchor, subject, program identity, manifest and byte digest; descendant receipt parent and event must agree
limits: This proves recorded causal ancestry within the host ledger; it does not assert that a newer receipt contains newer semantic model state.
Input signatures v1 authenticate input and structural manifest, not the active mutable checkpoint. A restore event is not a per-call producer signature.
Restore authorization is a coarse trusted host startup capability. Agents with access to that operation can select an older committed checkpoint.
The ledger and private checkpoint store remain host trust roots; their digests are not signatures or action authority.
Historical receipts without state ancestry remain readable; no ancestry is inferred for them.
At most 50000 restore events share the ledger's 32 MiB size cap. A crash before event commit may leave only an unreferenced checkpoint.
